chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

There is no problem with a man passing by fruit and eating from it, provided he does not spoil it. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade building walls in Medina in the places of passers-by. He said: 'And when a palm tree reached maturity, he ordered that openings be made in the walls in the places of passers-by.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jareer, from Abu Al-Rabie Al-Shamy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Similar to it, except that he said: 'And he should not spoil it, nor carry it away.'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for eating fruit from a tree along a public path according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the Islamic principle of public access to natural resources, balancing private ownership with communal benefit by permitting passers-by to consume fruit provided they do not spoil it or remove it entirely. The narration highlights the Prophetic precedent in Medina, where walls (*hitān*) were constructed with openings specifically to facilitate this access, reflecting a broader Shia legal emphasis on removing hardship (*raf' al-haraj*) in daily transactions. This ruling underscores the social responsibility of landowners to maintain transparency and accessibility in their properties.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no problem with the man who passes by upon the fruits and he eats from it, but he should not spoil (the fruits).

Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> had forbidden the building of the walls in Al-Medina in the place of the passers-by (footpaths), and when it was so that the palm tree reached (maturity), he<sup>saww</sup> ordered for the openings (to be made) in the walls in the places of the passers-by’.

Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Khalid Bin Jareer, from Abu Al Rabie Al Shamy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, similar to it except that he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And he should neither spoil nor carry (take away)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ’Isma‘il ibn Marrar from Yunus from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is not harmful if a man passes by fruits and eats from them but does not destroy them. The Messenger of Allah prohibited building walls in al-Madinah because of people passing by.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘When dates ripened, he (the Messenger of Allah) would command to make openings in the walls for the people passing by.’”
Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from abu al-Rabi’ al-Shamiy from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
a similar Hadith except that he (the Imam) said, ‘. . . does not destroy and does not carry.’”
